correctness.rationale: For the fixed labelled alphabet and fixed-point-free involution, the t leftmost complete greedy arches of the half-word and the t rightmost mirrored arches leave exactly R followed by its complemented reversal. Every family of at least 2t+1 complete disjoint blocks can have its outside t blocks on each side replaced by those greedy arches, since the left endpoints of the remaining region can only move left and its right endpoints can only move right. A complete block in the centre exists exactly when the residual support meets every involution pair; two such disjoint blocks are impossible because each must cross the central cut. The greedy characterization follows, for example, by using the arch-terminal letters in order followed by a letter absent from the remainder to witness non-universality at the next length. The geometric series uses q! S(n−1,q−1) arches of length n, and for support size s uses s! S(n,s) words per support; the orbit-covering proper supports number binom(p,s−p)·2^(2p−s). This verifies the GF, including the empty word and the binary specialization. Every h-universal word has at least h occurrences of each symbol, so equality at physical length qh forces minimum-size permutation arches, and for odd h a final p-letter remainder with one letter per pair. Index at equality cannot exceed h.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed. Its archived 35,856 half-word checks use whole-word arch index comparisons and test the direct subsequence definition only through target length 3 (or the smaller length bound). Coefficient DP assumes the central identity when it assigns indices; the analytic proof, not that DP, resolves the identity for unbounded lengths.

evidence: The finite-automaton counting theorem assumes an input regular language of whole words. Intersecting the entire fixed-point-free folded-word language with a* followed by bar(a)* gives the nonregular equal-run language.

The mixed-involution record assumes both fixed letters and transposed pairs and expressly excludes the no-fixed-letter endpoint. The remainder paper treats repetition/circular universality in the passages read.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither general scope contains this fixed-point-free distribution as a stated specialization. Running an automaton on half-words after discovering the orbit test is not a prior whole-word theorem evaluating the claimed coefficients.

value.rationale: Fixed points of reverse-plus-relabel symmetry form a natural constrained word class. The formula gives the entire exact-index distribution uniformly, distinguishing even and odd exact indices by pair coverage, and supplies exact minimum-length witness counts. Those are useful counts for the constrained class, not just the general minimum-length bound or a small table.
residual_risks: No claim about other involutions, quotienting words by symmetries, or applications outside abstract word combinatorics.
